policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere וּצְנִ֥יף and ketiv וצנוף are the same lexeme (6797); OSHB parses the qere as a construct noun and the ketiv as a qal infinitive absolute of the same root, but in construct with מְלוּכָה both yield the headdress. ASV "and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God" renders either reading, and no note is mapped here.
